problem: Consider the points $D(1,3,2)$, $E(t,2,4)$ and $F(3,t,3).$ Find $∠EDF$ given that $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=2.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=-4$, find the angle between $\mathbf{a}=\langle t, \, -2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 6, \, t \rangle$. Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
examples.worked_solution:
First, since $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=-4$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-4 \\ t\cdot 6+(-2)\cdot t & =-4 \\ 6t-2t & =-4 \\ 4t & =-4 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨-1,-2⟩,\,b=⟨6,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{37}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{185}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{185}} \right) \approx 107.1^\circ.
$$

feedback.problem: Find $∠XZY$ given the points $X(-2,1,0)$, $Y(-1,0,4)$, and $Z(-1,2,-2).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}x=⟨-2,1,0⟩,\,y=⟨-1,0,4⟩,\,z=⟨-1,2,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△XYZ$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠XZY=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045824/assets/87453fecb9da6b9e673ab5a85a289a3fac73f4fb90fc8f1b33e7c0a80b1ea77f.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ZX} & =x-z \\  & =⟨-2,1,0⟩-⟨-1,2,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{ZY} & =y-z \\  & =⟨-1,0,4⟩-⟨-1,2,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{ZX}\cdot \overset{\to }{ZY}}{|\overset{\to }{ZX}||\overset{\to }{ZY}|} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 6}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{40}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{240}} \\  & =\frac{14}{4\sqrt{15}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{15}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{7}{2\sqrt{15}})={25}^{∘}.
$$
